title: Continuity of rotation sensitivity at zero
statement: Let $n\ge 0$ and let $A\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be measurable. The rotation sensitivity of $A$ tends to $0$ as the real angle tends to $0$.
replaced: Let $n\ge0$, let $\gamma_n$ be standard Gaussian measure on $\mathbb R^n$, and let $G,G\prime$ be independent vectors with law $\gamma_n$. Write $s_A(t)$ for the real value of the product-measure mass $(\gamma_n\otimes\gamma_n)\{(g,h):\mathbf1_A(g)\ne\mathbf1_A(\cos t\,g+\sin t\,h)\}$. For any measurable $A\subseteq\mathbb R^n$, $s_A(t)\to0$ as the real angle $t\to0$.
